correctness.rationale: For every nonempty face, strict convexity and the KKT equations give the unique inverse-curvature minimizer. Its active gradient coordinates are equal and its inactive gradients vanish, so a standard simplex vertex oracle chooses an unseen vertex. The segment objective is an explicit strictly convex quadratic whose exact minimizer has weight a_j^{-1}/(Z_S+a_j^{-1}); substituting that value gives exactly the enlarged-face minimizer. Induction proves the finite-termination count. Exact-rational replay checks a representative chain and a finite stress family, while the all-dimensional claim rests on the analytic proof.

value.rationale: Positive diagonal quadratics over a probability simplex are natural weighted allocation models. Fully corrective Frank–Wolfe normally requires solving a growing active-set problem; on this whole family an ordinary exact segment line search performs that correction automatically. The resulting inverse-curvature active-set law, explicit gap/objective values, tie-order independence, and exact finite termination provide a reusable structural simplification rather than a routine numerical instance.
